title: Lessons from Generating 12 Trillion Synthetic Tokens — Bogdan Gaza, DatologyAI
talk_summary: DatologyAI's CEO describes engineering lessons from a 12-trillion-token synthetic data generation run: metadata fetching at S3 scale, GPU instability and checkpointing, cross-cluster CPU/GPU scheduling, and inference parameter tuning. The core transferable ideas are batching metadata calls, right-sized partitions with idempotent checkpointing, atomic CPU+GPU scheduling, and systematic hyperparameter sweeps for throughput.

takeaways.technique: Batch metadata/list calls instead of per-object requests
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of fetching S3 object metadata one request at a time (rate-limited, ~10ms each), they batch list requests up to S3's ~1000-per-page limit, cutting metadata population from days to hours.
takeaways.evidence_quote: instead of doing one at a time, you can batch them all together. S3 supports this through their APIs
takeaways.numbers: 11 days -> 2 hours of API processing time

takeaways.technique: Right-sized work units + idempotent checkpointing for long runs
takeaways.what_they_do: They shrink partitions so a node failure loses little work, and checkpoint partial progress back to durable storage with idempotent overwrite so retries resume instead of restarting.

takeaways.technique: Atomic scheduling of coupled CPU and GPU resources
takeaways.what_they_do: They decoupled CPU (Spark/Ray head) and GPU pools but schedule head+worker atomically with dedicated pools, avoiding the case where GPU capacity is available but CPU isn't (or vice versa).
takeaways.evidence_quote: you need to think about both your CPU and your GPU requirements in order to do this optimally

takeaways.technique: Systematic inference hyperparameter sweeps for throughput
takeaways.what_they_do: They run grid searches over batch size, speculative decoding, and other serving flags for their inference stack, treating batch inference differently from online serving.
takeaways.evidence_quote: about 40% throughput gains just by tweaking the flats for VLM

takeaways.technique: Unify research/experiment and production pipelines on one codebase
takeaways.what_they_do: They eliminated a two-track system (Slurm research cluster vs Kubernetes product pipeline) that caused manual data backfills, slow/error-prone work, and underutilized GPUs, moving everything onto one orchestrated path.
takeaways.evidence_quote: This was slow, errorprone, um, limited in velocity and kind of led to underutilizing our GPUs
